report_cohort_links.report_specific_population: 2 of 4 enrolled amateur runners whose PBMC samples passed both library-preparation QC and single-cell QC at both pre- and post-run timepoints; these 2 donors' paired data underpin all single-cell, pseudobulk DEA and GSEA results.
report_cohort_links.link_notes: Methods text gives two QC-exclusion statements that read as potentially distinct events: (i) §2.2 'Samples from one amateur runner did not produce libraries of sufficient quality and were thus excluded from the sequencing experiment'; (ii) §2.3 'Samples from one amateur runner did not have sufficient high-quality cells and were thus excluded from further analyses'. The main text never states the resulting final n. Supplement Table S2 (cell-type counts) lists exactly 4 samples (pre_1, pre_2, post_1, post_2), and their cell totals (299+1110+954+1848=4211) exactly match the reported 'total of 4211 cells... deemed high-quality' (p.3). This confirms n_analyzed=2 donors (paired pre/post), i.e. of the 4 enrolled, 2 were excluded in total – consistent with, but not proven identical to, the two methods-section sentences describing one exclusion each. Flagged as unresolved (see unresolved_questions).

_locators.n_analyzed: Supplement Table_S2 header row ('pre_1','pre_2','post_1','post_2'); p.3 §3 Results '4211 cells were deemed as high-quality'

measurements.platform: droplet scRNA-seq (ddSEQ/STARsolo/Seurat) aggregated per annotated cluster into pseudobulk counts; DESeq2 paired DEA per cell type (§2.5)
measurements.cell_context: 9 annotated clusters analysed separately (classical/non-classical monocytes, myeloid DC, NK, CD8+NKT-like, memory CD4+T, naive CD4+T, naive B, platelets)
measurements.assay_validity: QC: cells removed if UMI counts <200, gene counts <200, or >20% mitochondrial UMIs; genes not detected in ≥10 cells across the dataset discarded; batch/mitochondrial/cell-cycle effects corrected via Seurat SCTransform + IntegrateData (p.2 §2.3)
measurements.feature_identification: NR (final retained gene count after the ≥10-cell filter not numerically stated)
measurements.comparison: post-run vs pre-run, paired design, pre-run as reference level (DESeq2)
measurements.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across genes tested per cluster
measurements.confounding: batch effect, mitochondrial expression and cell-cycle effect modelled as confounders and corrected (p.2 §2.3)
measurements.donor_level_inference: Pseudobulk-per-cluster aggregation used specifically to avoid treating individual cells as independent biological replicates (p.2 §2.5); statistical unit = donor (n=2) per cluster.
measurements.missing_data: see sample_sets.missing_data (2 of 4 enrolled donors excluded before this analysis)
measurements.null_findings: No significantly modulated genes detected in myeloid dendritic cells or non-classical monocytes after multiple-testing correction (p.3 §3.1)
measurements.reported_feature_count: 23 DEGs in classical monocytes + 3 DEGs across lymphoid cell types (Table 1)
measurements.measurement_notes: This row is the assay-level tested-universe/approach summary for the cluster-resolved pseudobulk DEA (§2.5), the paper's primary 'single-cell analysis approach'. Named-candidate rows below cover a representative subset of the tabulated significant genes; full gene×cluster transcription of Tables 1/2/S1/S4 (dozens of rows) was out of scope for this pilot pass – see unresolved_questions.
measurements.tested_universe: All expressed genes detected in ≥10 single cells across the whole dataset, ranked by log2FoldChange, tested per annotated cluster via DESeq2 (negative-binomial model, paired design)

precision_validation.replication: No technical replicates, no repeat library prep, no spike-ins or reliability metrics (ICC/CV) reported.
source_locator: p.2 §2.2-2.3 (QC thresholds described; no reliability/replicate metrics reported)
precision_validation.evidence_notes: QC pipeline (UMI/gene/mito thresholds, batch correction) is described but no formal analytical-reliability statistic (repeat measurement, ICC, CV) is reported for the assay itself.

precision_validation.response_evidence: Pre-run baseline and a single immediate post-run (15-30 min after arrival) sample; both within the organising window (pre_exercise_baseline and 0_to_lt30min bins).
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Only one post-exercise time bin sampled (0_to_lt30min); no further recovery timepoints (e.g., 24-72h) to chart the return-to-baseline trajectory noted by the authors as a limitation relative to Yu et al. [14] (>24h to reach baseline, p.9).

9 immune/megakaryocyte cell types annotated via SCType marker database, giving cell-type-specific transcriptomic resolution; however an 'Unknown' cluster (substantial fraction, see Figure 3) and co-isolated non-leukocyte platelets reduce overall specificity.

precision_validation.individualization: No repeated-baseline or repeated-bout data; n=2 analysed donors; authors explicitly state the small sample 'might restrict the generalizability and reliability of the results' and call for inclusion of more individuals in future work (p.9).
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Individual-level variation is observed qualitatively (per-donor cell/gene differences implied by small n) but not quantified (no ICC/CV/response-heterogeneity statistic); authors frame results only as a 'complex dynamics attributable to different actors', not an individualised marker claim.

precision_validation.functional_evidence: No direct in vitro/ex vivo/in vivo immune-function assays performed; GO pathway enrichment (viral process, stress response, coagulation pathways) is annotation-level, not a measured function per the manual's rule.
precision_validation.evidence_notes: No clinical/infection follow-up and no functional assay; only transcriptomic/pathway-annotation evidence, interpreted narratively as supporting 'open window' or 'immunoenhancement' hypotheses.

precision_validation.replication: Single cohort, single report; no technical or biological replication beyond the paired n=2 donors. Authors narratively note concordance with prior literature (Yu et al. [14], Condeminas et al. [15], Maqueda et al. [29]) for specific genes/pathways, but this is cross-study narrative corroboration, not a formal independent validation of this report's candidates.
precision_validation.evidence_notes: No independent cohort or external dataset formally re-tests this report's specific DEGs/pathways; validation_split=none.

precision_validation.field_feasibility: 'we analyzed a small number of samples due to the high cost of single-cell sequencing' (p.9 Perspective) – explicit cost/throughput barrier reported for scRNAseq as a field method.
precision_validation.evidence_notes: Authors explicitly discuss cost as a practical constraint limiting sample size/throughput, a direct feasibility statement (not a formal field-use test).

eligibility_opinion.rationale: Single identifiable acute bout (21.1 km half-marathon, April 2019) with a pre-run baseline and an immediate post-run sample (15-30 min after arrival; p.2-3 §2.1), i.e. within the 0-72 h organising window with no exposure threshold required. Direct immune-cell transcriptome (scRNAseq of PBMCs; p.2 §2.1-2.4) satisfies the immune-linkage rule as immune_cell_omics.

unresolved_questions: Final analysed donor count (n=2) is only inferable by cross-referencing two separate QC-exclusion sentences in §2.2 and §2.3 with the supplement's sample list (Table_S2: pre_1/pre_2/post_1/post_2) and cell-count arithmetic (299+1110+954+1848=4211); the main text never states the final n explicitly, and it is not fully certain the two sentences describe two distinct runners rather than the same runner described twice. Manual should require reviewers to flag when final analysed n must be back-calculated from a supplement rather than stated directly.
Post-run sampling window ('15-30 min after arrival') straddles the 0_to_lt30min/30min_to_lt3h time_bin boundary; the manual does not specify how to bin a reported range that spans a bin edge.

marker_family vocabulary has no explicit category for non-leukocyte blood-cell transcriptome (platelets/megakaryocyte lineage); used 'other' for platelet CCL3/CCL4 rows but this is a judgement call, not a defined rule.

The omics 'record every named candidate regardless of significance' rule, combined with this report's multiple DEA approaches (cluster-resolved single-cell + whole-sample pseudobulk) and multiple tables (Table 1: 23 genes x up to 5 cell types; Table 2: 27 genes; Table S1/S4), implies dozens of measurement rows; this pilot recorded only a representative subset (assay-universe summaries + ~5 named-candidate examples) rather than every row, which is a feasibility/row-volume issue the manual should address for omics reports.
reports.version_date / version_label: no explicit online-first date or version label distinct from the Accepted date (7 Jan 2025) and issue pagination (e70018) is given in the text.
